title: Getting Started
paragraphs: Artisan Toolbox is a collection of focused Laravel packages and developer tools. Each package can be adopted independently, while shared foundations live in the Core package.
Requirements vary by package. Check the package page before installing it. The current package generation targets:
PHP 8.5 or later
Laravel 13 components
Composer 2
Packages are distributed through Packagist and installed with Composer:
Replace <package> with the package name, such as core or dump-to-console.

Packages with frontend features may also require an npm dependency. For QZ Tray Connector, install artisan-toolbox/qztray with Composer and register its bundled frontend using npm install ./vendor/artisan-toolbox/qztray, which records a file:vendor/artisan-toolbox/qztray dependency, and then follow its quickstart to configure credentials and Ziggy routes.
Read Choose a Package for a quick comparison, or browse the complete package catalog.

title: Documentation Policy
paragraphs: This repository is the source of truth for complete, user-facing Artisan Toolbox documentation.
Each package repository keeps a concise README containing:
the package purpose;
the installation command;
a minimal usage example;
compatibility and stability information;
links to this documentation, contribution guidance, security policy, changelog, and license.

Detailed guides, configuration references, troubleshooting information, and architectural explanations belong here. This separation keeps package landing pages useful without forcing maintainers to update the same long-form content twice.
The canonical public documentation URL is https://atb.dev.br. Each package README must link to its corresponding page under this URL.

Use contact@atb.dev.br for public contact metadata and security reporting. Transactional sender addresses and authentication fixtures keep their separate purposes. The replacement application's repeatable workspace contact check is documented in docs/documentation/quality.md; it does not inspect live credentials or modify dependency versions.

Start each package overview with its purpose, stability, and documented version. Follow with requirements, installation, a minimal example with an expected result, and links to detailed guides. For packages in development, describe the checkout and label examples as previews.

In the replacement application, maintain package names, summaries, versions, stability, and requirements in app/Documentation/Packages/. app/Documentation/Documentation.php owns the catalog. app/Documentation/PageSlug.php owns page identities and sidebar order. The home page, package catalog, and package chooser consume that shared catalog. The legacy publication keeps its catalog in docs_old/src/packages.mjs until cutover.

The replacement sidebar distinguishes section headings, package groups, and page links through typography, spacing, and nested guide lines. Highlight only the current page, allow long titles to wrap, and open the active branch automatically. Version badges use neutral colors. Development packages retain a visible stability label.

Use Tailwind utilities and the shared tokens consumed through Front Awesome's public CSS entry points in the replacement. DocsLayout and DocsNavigationItem own the sidebar. The legacy Astro publication alone keeps sidebar styles in docs_old/src/styles/custom.css, scoped to #starlight__sidebar, with Starlight owning its navigation. Keep keyboard focus visible and mobile touch targets at least 44 pixels high in both applications.
Before changing these styles, check a deeply nested guide such as PM2 configuration in both light and dark themes. Verify that:
the current page is distinguishable and its active branch is expanded;
Tab shows a visible focus outline, and Enter expands or collapses a focused group;
long labels and badges fit without horizontal scrolling at a viewport width of 390 pixels;
the mobile menu opens, scrolls to all links, and closes after a page is selected.

Use the Shields.io flat-square style and keep badges in this order: Release, PHP, Laravel, Node.js, Tests, and Docs. Use the GitHub release badge for published packages and an in development badge before the first release.

Show PHP and Laravel when they apply to the installation. Show Node.js when the package documents a supported frontend version range. Match the version constraints in the package manifests and keep all supported ranges visible. Point Tests to the package's GitHub Actions workflow and Docs to the package's canonical documentation page.
Update the badges in the package's readmeHead() method and run php vendor/bin/maintainer readme:update from its checkout. In the Maintainer source checkout, run php maintainer readme:update.

Document how to install Artisan Toolbox JavaScript packages from their Composer-installed directories using file:vendor/artisan-toolbox/<package> dependencies. Run Composer before the frontend package manager. Explain whether the application builds the source or imports an existing build.

Every package has an overview quickstart and a dedicated Installation page. Open the overview with the package's purpose, stability, and documented version. Follow with requirements, installation, a first working example, configuration, task guides, advanced explanations, reference, and development. Put configuration before the first example when that example requires it.

Order the sidebar by what readers need next. Prerequisites precede dependent guides, and lookup material follows guided use. Keep this editorial order in the owning registry. Do not alphabetize the menu or maintain another list in Vue.

State the starting environment and the directory where each command runs. Install the backend before its frontend dependency. Explain required sessions, authentication, broadcasters, workers, or hardware before using them. Mark optional integrations explicitly.

Each quickstart includes public API code with defined inputs and an observable expected result. Keep a short installation command in the overview and link to the complete procedure. A beginner must be able to reach the first result without discovering missing setup in an advanced guide.

Reserve the large package identity header for the overview. Child pages keep their task title and compact shared package tags. Documented compatibility and stability remain separate from the Composer version installed in the documentation application. Label local branches and unpublished APIs as previews.
Before completing a documentation task, check every affected package in both the legacy source and the Vue application:
Confirm the purpose, stability, documented version, requirements, and preview status against the package.
Follow the dedicated installation from its stated starting environment, with backend steps before frontend steps.
Run the first example with its documented inputs and compare the actual result with the expected result.
Follow the next guide and confirm that sidebar order places its prerequisites first.
Check that shared components own repeated presentation and that the task preserves existing examples, anchors, links, and advanced content.
Record the dependency refresh outcome and the checks that passed or remain blocked.

Use the versioned atb-documentation skill and its bundled writing and prose review guidance. Separate tutorials, task guides, reference, and explanations. The project follows Diataxis tutorial guidance for achievable first results and Google's procedure guidance for ordered actions and expected outcomes. Follow Google's code sample guidance with the project's language-specific formatting conventions.
An additional skill needs a concrete missing capability and a reviewed source. Reuse installed guidance rather than installing unknown external skill code that duplicates it.

Fix a defect at its owning source, whether that is a prerequisite, registry, public package API, or shared component. Do not hide defects with page-specific CSS patches, duplicated metadata, copied package internals, forced versions, weakened tests, or fixture refreshes that conceal missing content.

Use specialized shared components with explicit inputs for headers, requirements, prose, examples, callouts, and navigation. Inspect package exports before adding documentation behavior, then record the public export used or the concrete reason that the application owns it.

Each documentation task attempts compatible updates for installed Artisan Toolbox packages and the main runtime and test dependencies. Inspect the resolved versions, run Composer before npm, refresh Composer-delivered frontend copies, and run the affected checks. Record the commands, actual version changes, already-current results, conflicts, and unavailable registries or other blockers.

Stay within the declared compatibility constraints. Do not fabricate a version bump, force an unpublished preview into a stable requirement, or relax compatibility to claim that the refresh succeeded. An installed checkout is runtime evidence, not proof of a public release.

Documentation demos consume public package APIs. Vue demos belong under resources/js/components/demo/<package>/<section>/, and backend helpers belong under app/Demo/<Package>/<Section>/. Active connections, queues, jobs, and printing start only after the reader acts. Each demo provides loading, failure, reset, and source behavior. Private credentials remain on the server.

Comparisons between native Laravel or Inertia and Mosaicast use the same inputs, payloads, event counts, timing, session, and queue conditions. Show the observed delivery behavior and its limits. Do not invent performance claims or add infrastructure that the requested example does not need.

Each package owns agent guidance for using its public APIs in consuming applications. Keep its source under resources/boost/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md. Keep repository contribution rules in AGENTS.md.

Reuse an existing skill when the task fits. Match its directory and YAML name, and write a precise description for discovery. Teach supported prerequisites, installation, public API usage, expected results, and relevant limitations. Link to the canonical guides instead of copying complete reference material.

Keep the entry point focused. Add linked references or scripts only when a real workflow needs them. Verify that the supported Boost version distributes every required resource. Keep skills in the Composer archive and check discovery in a consuming Laravel application. Boost remains optional development tooling for consumers.

Consumers install the package through Composer before running php artisan boost:install and selecting skills for their agent. After package updates, php artisan boost:update refreshes selected resources. Verify new skill selection interactively when needed. Edit package sources and regenerate consumer copies.

Follow Add and maintain a package usage skill for an example, distribution checks, and consumer verification. The format and installation behavior follow Laravel Boost's third-party package skill guidance and OpenAI's skill authoring guidance.

The documentation repository owns a versioned bundle of atb-documentation and atb-package-development skills under documentation/agent-standards/. The bundle includes writing guidance and page patterns so contributors share a maintained standard without requiring personal skill installations. Repository-specific instructions and specialized package skills continue to govern their respective areas.

The documentation application is the first consumer. Its synchronizer installs the selected version into .ai/skills/ for Laravel Boost and .agents/skills/ for Codex, together with a lock and standalone checker. CI runs npm run standards:check before dependency installation. Other adopting projects can run node .ai/sync.mjs --check without a sibling documentation checkout.

Follow shared agent standards for installation and upgrades. Change the owning source, seal a higher version, synchronize the selected consumers, and review their diffs. Record projects still using older versions. Package usage skills under resources/boost/skills/ continue to serve developers adopting public package APIs.

Review affected skills whenever APIs, commands, configuration defaults, compatibility, prerequisites, failure behavior, or recommended usage change. Update instructions and examples in the same task as the implementation, tests, central guides, migrated pages, and changelog. Record why a reviewed skill needs no edit when its guidance remains accurate.

Validate metadata, links, resources, and executable examples. Check discovery and a realistic consumer task when adding or changing a skill. Include a request outside its scope to check the description. Record actual results and blockers. Passing a syntax check alone does not prove that the instructions work.

Use the versioned atb-documentation skill and its bundled writing and prose review guidance. Choose one Diataxis mode per guide, write clear English with active voice, and use exact public API names. Define example inputs, place prerequisites before use, show expected results, and preserve working links and anchors.
Before completing a change, review the following items:
Identify affected public contracts, supported versions, dependent packages, guides, and skills.
Update implementation, behavior tests, skills, canonical documentation, legacy pages, migrated pages, and changelogs together where affected.
Keep package READMEs concise. Update their installation command, minimal example, or compatibility statement only when affected.
Run relevant checks, executable examples, migration parity, and the required validation suites. Record checks that could not run and their exact manual follow-up.
Report affected repositories, compatibility implications, unchanged guidance, dependency refresh results, and remaining blockers for review.
Community-facing documentation is written in clear, inclusive English. Additional translations may be introduced later without changing the English source documentation.

The replacement's 1.x repository supplies the Vue source references shown in documentation page footers. Each registered page names its actual Vue file, and a registry test verifies that the source exists. The migrated Maintainer Code Quality section lives under /docs/maintainer/ci. The Configuration overview, reference, publishing guide, and SSH keys guide live under /docs/maintainer/configuration. Local migration does not imply production cutover.

Package guide pages reuse a shared header that keeps each guide title visible beside its package specifications. Package overview wordmarks do not replace detailed guide titles. Migrate related section pages together where practical, retaining code examples, anchors, exact legacy redirects, and destinations for guides that remain on this site.

The complete Versioning section is migrated under /docs/maintainer/versioning, including commits, HTML diffs, releases, and project integration. The pending-push feature is explicitly labeled as a preview on the current 1.x branch after 1.10.0. Preserve production-autoload discovery requirements even when integration classes are used only by development tooling.
The replacement's shared DocsLink opens external HTTP(S) destinations in a new tab with noopener noreferrer. Internal destinations, local anchors, email links, and telephone links retain their appropriate navigation behavior.

The replacement application provides operator access through /login using single-use email codes restricted to atb.dev.br. It uses SQLite-backed sessions and protects the Log Viewer UI, API, and downloads at /logs. Password, registration, dashboard, and settings endpoints are unavailable. Configure a real mail transport; login codes must never be written to logs. The full workflow lives in docs/documentation/access.md.

The workspace docs directory contains the replacement Laravel, Vue, and Inertia application. The existing site in docs_old remains the published content source until cutover. The replacement's authoring workflow, architecture, asset process, and staged migration plan live under docs/documentation in the workspace.

Keep package changes synchronized with this site and any corresponding migrated Vue pages during the transition. Migrate requirements, examples, heading anchors, and links before adding an exact legacy redirect. Unmigrated pages retain their current public URLs.

The replacement disables Vue SSR, uses JavaScript Vue setup components and Tailwind, and delegates documentation metadata to Laravel Head. Shared components own page headers, specifications, requirements, prose, code examples, and navigation. Browser icons and the manifest live under public/favicons/ in the replacement.

The replacement models visitable pages with a string-backed slug enum, immutable page and package definitions, and Laravel resources for frontend serialization. Named routes generate application URLs using APP_URL; published destinations for unmigrated guides stay on this site until their replacements exist.

Its navigation follows the nearest registered nonempty slug prefix. For example, maintainer/ci/quality belongs to maintainer/ci, under maintainer. Keep sibling order in the enum and do not maintain a separate Vue menu registry. The index remains a top-level link. Separate disclosure buttons expand sections; page links navigate and close the mobile menu. The active branch opens automatically, and only the current page receives current-page semantics. See docs/documentation/authoring.md for the authoring workflow.

Preserve space for nested labels, compact guide indentation, and distinct package sections in the replacement sidebar. Highlight only the current page, allow long titles to wrap, and retain 44-pixel touch targets. Review the actual application at desktop and mobile widths in both themes when changing this presentation.

Before implementing a documentation feature, inspect Artisan Toolbox's public components, composables, and backend APIs. Prefer consuming those capabilities over creating site-specific duplicates, and record the reuse decision in the same task. For example, inspect Front Awesome's Theme component and theme plugin before adding or changing theme selection. Consume its public @artisan-toolbox/front-awesome/tailwind.css entry point for shared tokens. Run php artisan vendor:publish --tag=front-awesome-branding to publish the application-owned resources/css/branding.css overrides and import them after the shared theme. Current checkout features may require a local preview until the package release publishes them. Follow the documented Composer-first consumer installation and use public package entry points.

Every package task must inspect and update the relevant content in this repository as part of the same change. This includes public features, bug fixes, commands, configuration, compatibility, workflows, extension points, architectural decisions, deprecations, migrations, and breaking changes.

Before a package task is complete, its documentation must accurately describe current behavior, examples, requirements, stability, and compatibility. Pull requests to this repository must pass content validation, formatting, and the production build.

The replacement application's composer ci:check runs a Rector dry run followed by Maintainer's complete PHP and frontend quality workflow. Development and CI use PHP 8.5 with Composer development dependencies installed. Maintainer and Deployer are development tools; the user owns deployment configuration and execution separately from the documentation migration.

The replacement's App\ArtisanToolbox implements Maintainer's public Versionable and WithReadmeHead contracts. It owns the application version and generated README metadata. After editing readmeHead(), run php vendor/bin/maintainer readme:update --no-interaction from the replacement checkout. Its isolated CLI regression test verifies production discovery, README synchronization, preserved manual content, and repeated execution.

The replacement application uses the 1.x branch for development and GitHub source links. Its tests workflow runs on pushes to 1.x and on pull requests. CI installs locked Composer dependencies before npm ci, builds client assets, and runs Rector and Maintainer as separate steps. Test services use array stores, synchronous queues, and SQLite in memory.

The replacement's .npmrc configures the scoped Web Awesome Pro registry and reads its authentication token from WEBAWESOME_NPM_TOKEN. Export the variable in the local shell before installing Pro dependencies. npm does not read Laravel's .env file. CI supplies the variable from a repository secret. The configuration enables install-links for local package dependencies and keeps dependency lifecycle scripts disabled.

The replacement generates its share image by resizing the wordmark before integer alpha flattening and explicit padding. Its asset tests verify exact blending, repeated generation, and matching SHA-256 digests for published artifacts. Keep these exact checks when changing the generator; the workflow is documented in docs/documentation/assets.md.

title: Versioning
paragraphs: The documentation site and the packages it documents have independent release histories.

The site follows Semantic Versioning. The replacement application's App\ArtisanToolbox::VERSION, in app/ArtisanToolbox.php, owns its current version. The class implements Maintainer's Versionable and WithReadmeHead contracts and stays in the production App\ PSR-4 directory so Maintainer can discover it. Its readmeHead() method owns generated README metadata. Keep the root package.json version synchronized when the configured release workflow updates frontend metadata.

The replacement currently develops on 1.x with an alpha version. This migration does not publish a release or change the production site. The legacy Astro publication retains its independent version in docs_old/package.json.
Patch releases correct or clarify existing documentation.
Minor releases add package documentation, guides, or site capabilities without removing established URLs.
Major releases may reorganize public URLs or remove documentation for unsupported package generations.

The replacement repository's existing tags use unprefixed versions, such as 1.0.0-alpha.1 and 1.0.0-alpha.2. Preserve that convention when preparing its next release. Package repositories keep their own tag conventions.

After editing readmeHead(), run php vendor/bin/maintainer readme:update --no-interaction from the replacement checkout. Keep manual README content outside the generated markers. The full application workflow lives in docs/documentation/quality.md in the workspace.
Every package follows its own version and compatibility policy. For a stable package, the badge in the navigation identifies the documented major generation.

Packages without a stable release use an In development label in the replacement and the WIP badge in the legacy publication. Their pages describe the development checkout and identify examples as previews.

For a stable package, the unversioned URL, such as /docs/core in the replacement or /packages/core/ in the legacy publication, documents the latest supported release. When a new major version requires substantially different documentation, the previous generation is preserved under a versioned URL before the unversioned page moves forward.
Documentation-only releases do not change any package version.

title: Choose a Package
paragraphs: Choose the package that solves your current task. Composer installs its PHP dependencies for you.
Core collects useful, focused helpers that do not need separate packages. Install it directly when you need its public APIs, or let Composer install it as another package's dependency.

Artisan Toolbox packages use Maintainer for their own maintenance, quality checks, and releases. We use and test these workflows in our projects. Maintainer can also be adopted independently for the same tasks. Its inclusion does not make it the implementation of a package's business features. Some production-autoloaded package identity classes implement its versioning and README contracts, so Composer installs Maintainer as a runtime dependency. Keep those declared dependencies available in production.

QZ Tray Connector ships its PHP backend and compiled frontend through Composer. Run Composer before the frontend package manager. Register the frontend with npm install ./vendor/artisan-toolbox/qztray, which records a file:vendor/artisan-toolbox/qztray dependency. Imports use @artisan-toolbox/qztray without an npm registry release. Printing requires QZ Tray on the user's computer and Laravel signing credentials; local previews do not require a QZ Tray installation. See the QZ Tray quickstart for installation and configuration.
